title: From Solver Trajectories to Teaching Trajectories: Cognition-Aligned Reasoning Distillation
topic: General Machine Learning->Transfer, Multitask and Meta-learning
claim: Training on trajectories containing failed reasoning steps consistently hurts accuracy, out-of-distribution generalization, and output efficiency compared to clean trajectories.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, horizontal bars with shared legend on top
description: A single row of three horizontal bar-chart panels, one per student model (Llama3.2-1B, Llama3.2-3B, Qwen2.5-7B), under a shared legend. The legend covers MATH 500 (dark blue), AMC23 (light blue), AGI-MATH (peach), ARC-Challenge (dark red) and Output Token Reduction (pink). Each panel has five bars extending from a vertical zero line, with bold value labels such as +5.05% and +1.19%. Nearly all bars point right, meaning the subset without failed steps does better. The pink token-reduction bar is longest in the 1B and 7B panels (about +5). The one exception is a small negative MATH 500 bar (-0.22) in the 3B panel. The x-axis runs from -2 to 6 with light dashed gridlines. The eye goes first to the long pink bars at the top of each panel.
caption: Motivating analysis of failed steps in trajectory-based reasoning distillation. Using DeepSeek-R1-generated DeepMath trajectories, we distill three student models on two 10,000-trajectory subsets under identical settings, where one subset consists entirely of trajectories with detected failed steps and the other consists entirely of trajectories without. Bars report the difference between the no-failed-step subset and the failed-step subset. Accuracy gains are reported in absolute points, while output-length reductions are reported as $(\mathrm{Token}_{\mathrm{failed}}-\mathrm{Token}_{\mathrm{no-failed}})/\mathrm{Token}_{\mathrm{failed}}\times100%$. Evaluation includes math benchmarks and ARC-Challenge for out-of-distribution generalization, and each panel corresponds to a different student model.
abstract: Knowledge distillation from large reasoning models (LRMs) often uses raw teacher trajectories as supervision. However, this practice creates a mismatch between the goal of distillation and the nature of teacher trajectories. Advanced LRMs typically improve their reasoning capabilities through reward-driven post-training, such as RLHF. This training optimizes them as strong solvers, rather than as teachers that produce reasoning processes smaller models can easily learn. Since smaller models have different "cognitive capacities" compared to their larger teachers, directly imitating raw teacher trajectories can sometimes be ineffective and often requires a substantial number of high-quality samples. To bridge this mismatch, we propose Cognition-Aligned Reasoning Distillation (CARD), an RL-based framework that transforms solver trajectories into teaching trajectories aligned with the student's cognition. Avoiding expensive resampling, our framework directly transforms existing trajectories. We optimize CARD with two reward signals: (1) a Distribution Alignment Reward that matches the student's predictive distribution, and (2) a Logical Coherence Reward that reduces misleading failed reasoning steps. Comprehensive evaluations across multiple student models and settings demonstrate that CARD outperforms distillation from raw teacher trajectories in in-domain settings while achieving substantial gains in out-of-distribution performance. Code is available at https://github.com/LiteSSLHub/CARD.
